lens: Untitled UI / Base UI polished SaaS: crisp, conventional, conversion-optimized
name: Quiet Coach Console
one_liner: A crisp, copy-in Untitled UI system where the live call becomes a private coach console with a rubric that moves as you talk, and the persona library and wizard make every sales job one click away.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the lens: a copy-in Untitled UI React kit (React Aria accessibility, Tailwind v4.3) for crisp, conventional chrome, one primary action per screen, and high-contrast forms. Changed three things after research: (1) Hyperbound's Live Call Coaching preview and Yoodli Coach show coaching as a nudge or playback, so the live call should be a console, not a chat; (2) the live stage uses a dark, low-glare canvas in both modes, since a light SaaS page distracts during a call; (3) the library and wizard borrow WRITER and Tines facets and HubSpot's stepper rather than generic cards. Self-assessed (the schema has no score field): A 7, B 7, C 5, D 5.3, E 5.4, F1 4, F2 6.5, F3 3.5 (1 = clearly worth building).

design_language.typography: Inter variable for UI and body: 16px body, 14px dense tables, 16px minimum on mobile inputs to stop iOS zoom. Sora 600 for H1 and H2 only, H1 40/48 on desktop and 30/36 on phone. Tabular numerals on every score, timer and percentile.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 12px cards, 10px inputs and buttons, full-round chips. 1px line borders and one shadow-xs on cards; no blurred orbs or glass. Focus ring 2px brand with 2px offset.
design_language.motion: 150ms ease-out for hover and state. Cue cards enter from the rail edge in 200ms, max two visible, older ones collapse into a count. Rubric bars ease over 400ms on change. Everything becomes instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke. Primary actions always pair icon and label. No emoji in product UI. Role and objection tags use a colored dot plus text, never color alone.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default; dark follows prefers-color-scheme with a toggle. Dark tokens: canvas #0B1220, surface #111A2B, line #22304A, ink #E6EDF7, brand #60A5FA. The live stage stays dark in both modes so the call canvas reads the same.

navigation_and_ia: Top nav: Practice, Library, Create, Progress, and Team (org roles only); Settings sits in the avatar menu. Practice runs pre-call briefing, live call and debrief as one flow with a step bar. Create is the AI persona wizard and also opens from the Library empty state. A Cmd-K palette (React Aria listbox) jumps to any persona or starts a call. On phone, a bottom bar holds Practice, Library, Create (centre, brand colour), Progress and More. Old URLs redirect: /trainer to Practice, /trainer/scenarios to Library, /dashboard to Progress. Login, MFA and the access-code gate keep their routes and are restyled.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Coaching runs as a second, silent model. After each rep turn, a coach call (an OpenAI model with structured JSON output) reads the last turns and returns a cue type, the current talk-track step, objection flags and provisional rubric scores, each tied to transcript turn IDs. The caller persona stays forbidden to coach, so cues are visual only and never leak into the call. Updates debounce to one per rep turn, target under two seconds after the rep stops talking, and cap tokens per call. Coach level (Silent, Light, Full) sets how many cues show. Live scores carry a 'Provisional' tag; the debrief re-grades with the full grader using the same rubric schema, so live and final numbers are comparable. Per-call cost is shown.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships as plain persona-and-scenario packs (one file per pack, schema-checked), so the open-source core has a real catalog: SDR cold calls, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success and collections. Facets: role, industry, difficulty, objection type, source and channel. Community packs carry a Community badge and a schema-check badge. The wizard takes a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or a pasted call, drafts buyer, scenario, talk track and rubric, shows the source sentence behind each field, and runs a 60-second test call before save. Its output is a contribution file ready for a pull request.
signature_moments: The rubric meter moves as you speak, tagged Provisional, with evidence dots that jump to the exact turn.
The talk track checks itself off in the left rail while the caller is still talking.
A 'Next best question' card appears only when the rep goes quiet or skips a discovery step.
Pre-call objection cards give a 10-second prep line for each likely pushback.
The wizard ends in a 60-second test call, so every new persona is tried once before it is saved.
The debrief's 'Practice next' card links to the exact library persona that targets the weakest criterion.
Every surface shows which OpenAI model did the work and what the call cost.
openai_fund_angle: Show OpenAI models in the product, not only in the README. The stage shows which model runs each job (caller, coach, grader, wizard) with per-call cost, and Settings lets a user swap models with their own key. Add the OpenAI Realtime API as a voice engine next to ElevenLabs so the demo can run on OpenAI voice end to end; this is engineering work, not in the repo today. For contributors: the wizard exports a persona pull request, the README gives a Codex CLI route to add a persona, 'good first persona' labels mark easy entry points, and a Contributors wall sits in Library. If Codex reviews persona PRs or drafts release notes, say so on the README and the Contributors page; that is the evidence the Codex for Open Source program asks for.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about a week): move to Tailwind v4.3 with tokens in CSS @theme; keep old pages behind a flag. Phase 1: copy the Untitled UI React primitives into the repo and retire .card and .btn-primary. Phase 2: new shell, Library (facets over the built-ins plus JSON packs), Pre-call briefing and Progress. Phase 3: coach service (structured-output coach call, cue schema, provisional rubric), the live console and the mobile sheet. Phase 4: wizard, debrief re-skin, manager view and team data. Keep /trainer, /trainer/debrief/[id] and /dashboard with redirects. Scenarios stay in localStorage until the Prisma store covers libraries. Ship each phase behind a flag and run a visual regression pass on all nine screens.

risks: Scope: this is XL. The coach service and persona packs are the long pole, not the visuals, so ship in phases behind flags.
Generic-look risk: Untitled UI is widely used. Keep the coach rail, rubric meter, evidence chips and persona cards bespoke so category C does not read as a template.
Cost and latency: a coach call on every rep turn adds spend. Debounce, cap tokens, show per-call cost, and keep BYO key as the default.
Tailwind 3 to 4 churn across globals.css and tailwind.config.ts; plan a visual regression pass before cutover.
License: confirm the Untitled UI copy-in terms before vendoring. Base UI is the fallback.

Business: F1 SaaS is crowded (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli, Outdoo AI and Mindtickle all sell live roleplay). The defensible angle is open persona packs plus BYO model. Licensing vertical packs to training companies and call centres (F2) is the stronger play.
Persona quality: community packs can encode stereotyped or inaccurate buyers. Add a review label and a schema and tone check before a pack is listed as Official.
Voice engine: today's voice is ElevenLabs. Adding OpenAI Realtime is a new integration and should be scoped separately.
